This edge cuts silk, bone and a bad mood!
Magic? No idea. But it glows and people step aside. Good enough!
Dwarf-made. Or made by someone who has seen a dwarf. Details!
This saved three men. The fourth didn't buy. Poor soul.
The smell? That's patina! Patina is history and history is expensive!
Hold it. Feel that weight? That's the weight of not dying!
A king wore this. Briefly. But he wore it!
This will outlive you. Literally. You go, it stays, someone buys it again!
Closing up shop: Buy something or get the hell out! We're closed!
Shop's closed! Take your coin and your smell elsewhere!
Closing time, last chance to overpay! No? Then shoo!
Everybody out! The shutters bite after dark, I'm not kidding!
We're closed! Come back tomorrow with more money and fewer questions!
Door's that way, mind the trap! No refunds on limbs!
Out, out, out! The shop is closed, and the shop's owner needs a nap and a drink!
Everybody out before the shutters drop — they drop fast, and I don't sweep up fingers!
Closing time! Buy something on your way out or leave faster — those are the options!
Shoo, shoo! Even I have to sleep, and the mimics get hungry after dark!
Closing! Come back at dawn and bring more gold than today!
The shop closes, the dreams stay. So do the prices.
Out, out! Even a merchant must sleep and count.
Last buyer, last discount, then the lamps go out!
One more thing, fine! But quickly, before I change my mind!
Tomorrow, friend. Tomorrow it'll cost more, so rise early.
I close, you leave. The money may stay, the money is welcome.
Go to bed and dream of that sword. You'll come for it in the morning.
Suspicious offer: Psst, want a map? Its last owner won't be needing it.
Under the counter I've got a ring. Don't ask whose finger.
This potion's totally safe, mostly! Sign here, here, and here.
Interested in a sword that whispers? It only whispers nice things, probably.
Special item, back room, no questions, no receipts, no witnesses.
Cursed? Who said cursed? It's spirited, half price, cash only!
Psst — interested in a ring that whispers? Ignore the whispers, they're mostly about you.
I've got a map to buried treasure — the treasure's mine, but the map's yours for fifty!
Care for a potion of unknown effect? The last buyer was thrilled — or was it screaming?
This amulet is definitely not cursed, and I'll say that as many times as you need!
I never sold this to anyone. To you, yes. Don't ask why.
No questions, no names, no receipt. Classic, between friends.
It came in at night. It leaves now. You never saw it.
It doesn't always work. But when it works, it works enormously.
Papers? It has papers. They're forged, but they're pretty.
I shouldn't be showing you this. So look well while I wrap it.
You buy it and you forget me. That's part of the price.
If anyone asks, you bought it from a tall man. Dark hair. Wasn't me.
Not selling that: I am not selling you that.
No. That one is not for sale. Not for gold, not for your soul.
That? You could not buy that. Not you, not your grandmother.
Forget it. That piece goes in the coffin with me.
For that I would not give you a bent copper. Take it or leave it.
Not that. That stays here, even for a cart of gold.
That isn't stock. That's a memory. I don't sell those.
No. No. And if you ask a third time, still no.
For that you'd have to bring me my brother. Alive. So, no.

Greeting: Well, shit, another adventurer. Wipe your boots before you come in.
Welcome, stranger. Coin first, questions later, blood never.
Oh good, you look expensive. Come in, come in.
Hello there. Don't touch anything, and we'll get along fine.
New face! Try not to die before you pay your tab.
Evening, traveler. Sword stays sheathed and the ale stays cheap.
Welcome, traveler! Wipe your boots — the floor remembers every sin dragged across it.
Ah, a new face! Sit anywhere you like — except the chair the cat has claimed.
Greetings, stranger! You look like trouble — the good kind, I hope, the paying kind.
Well met, adventurer! Half the town has been waiting for someone like you — the other half is hiding.
Good day. Strangers are rare here, and not always welcome.
Evening. If you want a bed, the inn is round the corner.
Well met. Keep your hands where I can see them.
Welcome to the village. We haven't much, but it's ours.
You're from the city. I can tell by the boots.
Late travellers are always looking for something.
Greetings, sirs. And ladies. Forgive me, my eyes are poor.
Gods keep you. Somebody ought to.
Warning: Don't go past the old mill. Nobody comes back with legs.
Bridge is out. The troll under it, sadly, is not.
Whatever you do, do not drink from the north well.
Bandits on the east road, ugly ones. Take the long way.
Something in that cave has been eating goats. Big goats.
Stay off the north road after dark. The wolves are hungry — and they've started working together.
Don't drink from the old well. The last one who tried now answers only to the moon.
Mind the bridge — it holds three travelers, or one traveler with a guilty conscience.
Something's stirring in the mines. The miners came up early — and the rats came up first.
Careful in the swamp. Everything there wants to eat you — even the flowers, especially the flowers.
Don't go into the woods after dark. That's all I'll say.
Two bells, lock your door. Three bells, run.
That road is shorter. So is life on it.
Don't drink from that well. People have been sick since they threw something in.
The reeve is asking about strangers. I never saw you, understood?
Go around that house. Nobody lives there and yet it's lit.
If you meet a man with a seal, say nothing. Not about me either.
Take torches. More than you think you need.
Town gossip: The baker's been sneaking out to the miller's every damn night.
Heard the mayor's new beard is actually glued on. I swear it.
The blacksmith's wife left him for a bard. A bard!
Priest got caught skinny-dipping in the holy font. Again.
Old Marta swears her cow's been possessed. Cow seems fine, honestly.
Someone's been stealing underwear off every washing line in town.
The mayor bought a new hat. Nobody knows where the gold came from — the hat certainly isn't talking.
The baker and the blacksmith are feuding again. This time it's over a goat — the goat seems flattered.
They say the priest gambles at night. Mind you, they also say the priest wins — suspiciously often.
Old Marrow's chickens have stopped laying. Marrow blames the witch — the witch blames the chickens.
They say the miller's wife is no widow. They say he comes home. At night.
The smith stopped taking work. Nobody knows why and he won't say.
A man with gold turned up at the inn. He left without the gold or his boots.
The children talk about a light on the hill. The grown-ups pretend not to see it.
The tax clerk has been here twice this month. That isn't normal.
They say somebody lives in the old tower again. I don't go up there.
The priest left and the chapel stands open. That isn't done.
They say the caravan didn't vanish. They say somebody let it go.
Quest offer: Rats in my cellar, big bastards. Fifty gold if they vanish.
My goat wandered into the crypt. Fetch it and I'll pay.
Need a package delivered. Don't open it, don't ask, don't die.
Someone's got to clear that ogre off the road. Feeling brave?
Lost my wedding ring down the outhouse. Pays surprisingly well.
There's a wolf eating my chickens. Kill it, keep the pelt.
I need a package delivered to the tower. Don't open it, don't shake it — and don't let it hum.
Fifty gold to find my missing cousin. A hundred if you bring them back sober.
Wolves are terrorizing the farms. Clear them out — the sheep will be grateful, in their way.
Escort my caravan to the pass. Pay is good, food is better — the bandits, sadly, are excellent.
I'll pay if you bring back what they took. No questions.
There's something moving in my cellar. I want it to stop moving.
My brother left a week ago. Find him. Even if he's dead.
I need an escort to the city. The road is bad and I'm old.
A wolf is taking our sheep. Bring the pelt, take the silver.
Clear the well and the whole village owes you. That's worth more than gold.
Someone robs the chapel at night. You catch him, I can't.
Carry a letter to the next village. Don't read it. I mean it.
Tavern talk: Another round? 'Course you do, your liver's not my problem.
Bard's on again tonight. Bring earplugs or more ale.
Best stew in town, mostly because it's the only stew.
That drunk in the corner claims he killed a dragon. Twice.
Don't sit there, that stool's got a curse and a wobble.
Ale's cheap, the stew's hot, and the gossip's free. Cheers.
Another round! My coin's good tonight — tomorrow it belongs to whoever I owe.
This ale tastes like it was brewed in a boot. A good boot, mind you — I'd drink it again.
Once fought a troll with nothing but a spoon. Lost the spoon, kept the story — fair trade.
The bard's on their third song about heartbreak. Any more and the whole tavern will need healing.
Another? Another. I'll regret both tomorrow.
Sit down. Gossip goes better at a table than in the street.
This ale is weak, but it's cheap, and so am I.
I played cards with that man. Never won. Never paid.
The musician is terrible, but he's loud. That counts here.
Want to know something, buy the innkeeper a drink. Not me, I talk free.
It used to be merrier here. Or I was younger.
Your health. Mine went long ago.
Farewell: Safe travels. Try to come back with all your limbs.
Off you go then. Don't die, you still owe me.
Farewell, friend. Mind the ditch on your way out.
Go on, get. And send more paying customers my way.
Good luck out there. Honestly, you'll bloody need it.
See you next time, if there is a next time.
Safe travels! Come back with gold, or come back with stories — both spend here.
Off you go, then. Try not to die — it's terrible for repeat business.
Farewell, friend! Keep your blade sharp and your wits sharper — one of them will rust anyway.
Go on, the road's waiting. It's been waiting for years — it's very patient, unlike me.
Go with the gods. And quickly, while there's light.
If you come back, bring news. It's the one coin we're short of.
Farewell. We'll leave the door unbarred as long as we can.
May the road be kind. And short.
Go. And forget what I told you.
Keep your wits. This is no country for the careless.
Goodbye. Or not, as it usually goes.
If you find my brother, tell him he's forgiven.
Piss off: Leave me be, before someone hears you.
Clear off. I have neither the time nor the mood for you.
No. Clear off before I call the others.
Get away from me and don't come back.
Out. I've no words for you and no time.
This street doesn't want you. Nor do I.
